messages:
alex_support: FYI customer 'BrightCart' opened a support ticket — their dedicated pool is serving a lot of 429s and high tail latency since last night's plan migration. They say it started ~02:00 UTC. attaching customer repro and a short trace :frowning:

sara_cs: Thanks. Customer repro steps they shared: 1) authenticate with API key, 2) send steady stream of small chat requests (avg 60 req/min), 3) saw 5xx/429 spikes and per-call latency jumped from 120ms -> 800ms. They included a short curl log and sample headers.

josh_oncall: Can you paste the tenant id + pool id here and any sample X-RateKey headers? I'll pull the pool metrics. :eyes:

alex_support: tenant=brightcart-prod, pool=reserved-eu-02, sample header: X-RateKey: tenant:brightcart-prod:rp42. Last 30s of logs attached below (sanitized).

--- logs ---
[2026-03-16T01:58:12Z] svc=frontend tenant=brightcart-prod route=/v1/chat status=200 latency_ms=115
[2026-03-16T02:00:03Z] svc=frontend tenant=brightcart-prod route=/v1/chat status=429 reason=quota_exceeded ratekey=rp42 latency_ms=12
[2026-03-16T02:00:08Z] svc=frontend tenant=brightcart-prod route=/v1/chat status=503 reason=queue_overflow latency_ms=820
--- end logs ---

maria_engineer: Quick hypothesis: quota config migration might have flipped the denom (minutes -> hours) or converted units incorrectly, which would reduce the allowed per-minute throughput by ~60x. Can someone confirm the effective rate profile for rp42 after last night's plan sync?

kevin_infra: Pulling mapping now. I see plan-sync job ran at 2026-03-16T01:55:00Z. The conversion script had a fallback that sets denom to "hour" when a missing field is encountered. Noted.

maria_engineer: That matches. If the tenant was operating on a per-minute limit and now the system interprets it as per-hour, they'll hit early 429s while being in a dedicated pool — autoscaler sees high usage and starts throttling to pool-level rules. Also noisy neighbors could push queueing up while this tenant's effective rate is tiny.

josh_oncall: Can we verify the quota entry? kevin, can you paste the quota key from the datastore (redacted)? If it's denom=hour we can confirm the bug.

kevin_infra: Found entry: {"tenant":"brightcart-prod", "rate_key":"rp42", "units":100, "denom":"hour"} — original expected denom was "minute". Looks like the migration didn't set denom correctly for some legacy plans.

maria_engineer: Ok that's the root cause. Immediate mitigation options: (1) patch quota denom back to "minute" for the affected tenant(s), (2) increase temporary pool override to avoid throttling, or (3) roll back the plan-sync migration. I recommend (1) + (2) short term.

kevin_infra: Agreed. I'll run a targeted patch for brightcart-prod now. Command I will use: 

```bash
curl -X PATCH https://internal-api/config/quotas/brightcart-prod/rp42 \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN' \
  -d '{"denom":"minute"}'
```

kevin_infra: Patch applied at 2026-03-16T02:10:12Z. Confirmed datastore entry now shows denom="minute".

deploy-bot: service/plan-sync-job v2.14.1 rolled back to v2.14.0 by @kevin_infra at 2026-03-16T02:11:05Z. CI job id: #8472.

maria_engineer: I've watched the metrics for reserved-eu-02: brightcart's 429 rate dropped to near zero within two minutes after the patch. Latency for their calls returned to ~130ms median. Queue depth normalized.

alex_support: I'll inform the customer and close the escalation if they confirm recovery. Sara, can you send a short note with the repro and the fix so we can include in the ticket? :thumbsup:

sara_cs: On it. Drafting now and will include the mitigation + ask them to confirm traffic is normal.

josh_oncall: Postmortem action items: 1) add a CI assertion to plan-sync to validate denom presence and mapping, 2) audit other tenants for missing denom values, 3) add an alert for sudden denom flips causing effective rate drops. Filing follow-ups.

alex_support: Thanks team. Closing thread when customer confirms.
